geo_headlines: AMAZON AND INTEL HIT TECH. **Nasdaq 100 futures 28,841 (-2.4%) and S&P 500 futures 7,668.75 (-1.1%) as Amazon fell 6% on an earnings miss and negative free cash flow, and Intel fell 21% on weak guidance; Dow futures roughly flat (CNBC, Investing.com).** Thursday Alphabet had its worst day ever, losing more than $500 billion in market value (Investing.com).

HORMUZ: MORE TANKER ATTACKS. Iran said four tankers struck mines; UKMTO reported a small boat attached two explosive devices to a tanker 25 nautical miles northeast of Khasab, Oman, disabling it, crew safe (CNBC). Central Command says the main routes are cleared of mines; the IRGC disputes it. The WSJ says the top regional commander briefed Trump on Iran options; Qatari mediators returned to Tehran Friday (Reuters).

OIL UP, GOLD DOWN. January Brent $113.65 (+2.6%) and December WTI $104.27 (+2.2%), lifted by the tanker attacks, a US crude draw and a Norway strike (BusinessDay); December Brent expires today near $116.73 (FT). Gold $3,986 (-1.1%).
CRYPTO: BINANCE HACK. Binance said $6.3 billion was stolen in what it called the largest attack in the industry's history (Investing.com). Bitcoin $77,706.85, after a 4.2% drop Thursday (TokenPost).

ASIA DOWN, BOJ HOLDS. Nikkei -2.1% and Kospi -3.5%; Hang Seng rallied late (CNBC). The Bank of Japan held at 1.25% with one vote for a hike, said inflation has roughly reached 2%, and will speed up ETF sales; December is live (Reuters). Stoxx 600 -0.25%, tech -2% (Reuters).

DATA: STRONG GROWTH, STICKY INFLATION. Thursday: Q3 GDP +3.4% versus 3.1% expected; September core PCE 3.1% year over year, in line; claims 194,000 (CNBC). FedWatch as of Thursday: December hike 74.4%, down from 85.3%. 10-year 4.98%, 2-year 4.61% (Treasury). Today: employment cost index 8:30 AM.
client_frame_short: Tech is under pressure this morning: Nasdaq futures are down more than 2% after Amazon and Intel disappointed, following Alphabet's record one-day drop Thursday. **This is a repricing of how fast AI spending pays off, not a broad economic scare: GDP grew 3.4% last quarter, the Dow is roughly flat, and bonds are rallying.** For clients: the S&P 500 is only about 1% below its high going in, broad portfolios are cushioned by bonds and non-tech stocks, and this is exactly the kind of week that disciplined rebalancing is for.
client_frame:
If a client calls this morning, the story is a sharp tech selloff driven by earnings, with the rest of the market and the economy holding up.

What changed overnight: Amazon fell about 6% after missing profit and revenue estimates and reporting negative free cash flow from AI spending, even as its cloud business grew at its fastest pace in years. Intel fell about 21% on weak guidance. Nasdaq 100 futures are down about 2.4% and S&P 500 futures about 1.1%, while Dow futures are roughly flat. Separately, crypto exchange Binance reported a $6.3 billion theft, and Iran said four more tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Oil rose about 2.5%.

Where we stand: Thursday the S&P 500 slipped 0.3% and the Nasdaq Composite 1.4%, led by Alphabet's worst day ever. Even so, the S&P 500 closed about 1.3% below its October 6 record close. GDP grew a strong 3.4% in the third quarter, core inflation held at 3.1%, and jobless claims stayed near historic lows. Treasury yields fell, with the 10-year back below 5%, and December hike odds dropped to about 74%.

Why it matters: investors are no longer paying for AI spending on faith; they want to see cash returns. Microsoft passed that test this week; Alphabet, Amazon and Intel did not. The selling is concentrated in the largest tech names, and bonds are doing their job as a cushion. This is the kind of week where an index-concentrated portfolio feels it, and a diversified one much less.

For clients: stay invested, rebalance toward targets, and use tech weakness to trim overweight positions back to plan rather than to sell in a hurry. What would change the view: a 10-year close above 5.40% (Thursday 4.98%), a 30-year above 5.75% (Thursday 5.32%), or US strikes on Iran that keep Brent well above $105 (January Brent now $113.65). Brent is there; strikes are the missing piece, and the timing still points to after November 3.
